newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Eight million rats get the chop in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Eight million rats get the chop in Vietnam.

text.p: Eight million rats have been killed in Vietnam's northern province of Thai Binh since last October following the launch of a cash-for-rodents campaign.
"The campaign has attracted people of different ages, from children to old people," said Dinh Van Hoa, vice-director of the province's plant protection department.
"Later they could sell rat's tails at 200 to 300 dong (1.7 to 2.5 U.S. cents) each at collection points," he added.
He said the dead rat tally during the province's winter-spring rice harvest was up from 2.6 million last year, although he gave no details of who did the counting.
Communal purges on rodents, which eat staple crops such as rice and sweet potatoes, are common in Vietnam.
